transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Lucas (Redwood SE), Sofia (Montara Head of ML), Daniel (Infra Lead), Priya (PM)

Summary (auto): Quick scoping for a POC focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling for Montara Bank's customer support and transaction review assistant. Discussed QPS, concurrency, token distributions, latency SLOs, data residency (on-prem), and benchmark plan.

[00:00:05] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros — i'll be the AE on this, lucas is our se. montara, could you do a quick 1-line on the project?
[00:00:18] Sofia: Sure, thanks Aisha. We're building an LLM-backed assistant to surface transaction context and answer compliance questions for support agents. Primarily internal use first, might expand to customer-facing messaging later.
[00:00:31] Priya: yes, product goal is to reduce average handle time and surface high-confidence recommendations to agents. security & data residency are non-negotiable.
[00:00:38] Lucas: Great, our focus today is workload sizing — qps, concurrency, input/output token distributions — so we can propose the right POC and benchmark plan.
[00:00:48] Daniel: quick note — we have an isolated datacenter and also cloud for non-sensitive stuff. for regulatory reasons we're leaning private (VPC/on-prem) for the POC if possible.
[00:00:58] Aisha: Understood. First question: what's your expected traffic profile? peak qps, average, typical concurrency?
[00:01:06] Sofia: We have two flows: agent assist (internal) and async summary for audit. Agent assist is bursty during business hours. average QPS today for the microservice is ~30, peak around 180 for short spikes. concurrency of live sessions around 25-40 depending on shift.
[00:01:28] Priya: those spikes happen at 11am and 3pm daily. The audit summarization runs nightly at lower qps.
[00:01:36] Lucas: ok that's helpful. do you have token distributions — like median input tokens and output length?
[00:01:42] Sofia: median input is around 40 tokens (short prompt with transaction context), 90th percentile ~180. outputs vary — for agent assist we expect concise replies, median 60 tokens, p95 ~220. for audit summaries, outputs can be longer 400-800 tokens.
[00:02:00] Aisha: so we'd model two workload shapes: low-latency, short outputs (agent assist) and batch, long outputs (audit). Good. What are your latency SLOs? p95, p99 targets?
[00:02:12] Daniel: For agent assist we need p95 < 350ms, p99 < 800ms ideally. Audit jobs are fine to be minutes.
[00:02:21] Lucas: p95 < 350ms for median 60 token output is tight but achievable with right model + deployment. Do you have a cost target for hosted vs dedicated?
[00:02:31] Priya: We need ballpark numbers to build a business case. Hosted is easier but we worry about data residency. Dedicated or on-prem is preferred if cost delta is within 2x of hosted.
[00:02:44] Aisha: We'll include cost modeling in the SOW. For now, let's focus on throughput. For agent assist with peak 180 qps and concurrency 40, are those simultaneous live completions or total requests?
[00:02:55] Sofia: peak 180 qps is total requests across the system, concurrency of 40 live agent sessions hitting the LLM concurrently. many requests are short context lookups.
[00:03:06] Lucas: For sizing we'll estimate tokens/sec. Example: if median input 40 tokens + median output 60 tokens = 100 tokens per request. At 180 qps that's 18k tokens/sec. For model selection we need to know tokenization model but this is a good approximation.
[00:03:24] Daniel: note that many requests hit the same customer KV cache/context; caching could reduce compute significantly if prefix KV caching is effective.
[00:03:33] Lucas: yes — we plan to model cache hit rates. Can you estimate what percent of requests reuse recent context?
[00:03:39] Sofia: roughly 30% exact reuse (same conversation), another 25% similar context where partial caching helps. so effective cache hit maybe 45-55% depending on TTL.
[00:03:52] Aisha: good. we'll include scenarios: no cache, 50% cache, 75% cache.
[00:03:59] [00:04:00] Speaker 1: (mumbled) is there any GPU constraint on your side — like on-prem nvidia models?
[00:04:05] Daniel: we have a small cluster: 4 x A100 40GB and some T4s for lightweight work. We can provision a few more if needed but want to see numbers first.
[00:04:15] Lucas: perfect — that lets us run an on-prem benchmark with similar hardware. For model selection, are you open to quantized open models or do you require a proprietary model?
[00:04:25] Sofia: open models are fine if quality meets a threshold. our success criteria will include correctness on a curated prompt set and a quality score above our baseline (we'll share).
[00:04:34] Aisha: let's define success criteria — we typically use three axes: latency SLOs, quality (accuracy/metrics on eval prompts), and deployment stability. does that align?
[00:04:44] Priya: yes. specifically: p95 < 350ms for agent assist, quality > 92% on intent extraction + factuality metric > 90% on our evaluation prompts, and no more than 2% error/fallback rate over a 1-week run.
[00:05:00] Lucas: noted. we'll create a benchmark sheet with those metrics.
[00:05:06] [00:05:10] Speaker 2: (crosstalk) do we need SOC2/iso stuff?
[00:05:13] Aisha: we will share our security packet (SOC2 report, penetration test summary, SSO/SAML docs, KMS integration notes). For on-prem we support customer-managed KMS/HSM.
[00:05:25] Daniel: good — we'll need to see audit logs and explainability for model outputs for compliance.
[00:05:31] Lucas: Redwood's console includes request-level tracing and token-level cost breakdowns; we can enable extended audit retention for the POC if needed.
[00:05:40] Sofia: timeline — we'd like a 4 week POC: week 1 baseline data & infra setup, week 2 benchmarks and tuning, week 3 run longer stability tests and evaluate quality, week 4 wrap and decision. is that feasible?
[00:05:53] Aisha: yes that's our normal cadence. We'll do an on-prem benchmark in week 2.
[00:05:59] Lucas: For benchmarks we'll run these scenarios:
- Agent assist low-latency: median request 100 tokens, concurrency scenarios 10, 25, 40; target p95 measured.
- Cache impact: 0%, 50%, 75% effective cache.
- Model variants: quantized 7B, 13B, and 70B distilled to compare quality vs latency.
- Audit batch: large output length tests 400-800 tokens, throughput measured in qps for batch jobs.

[00:07:05] Daniel: question on the cache — does Redwood support KV caching on private deployments?
[00:07:10] Lucas: yes, our runtime supports prefix and KV cache; there may be slight differences on kernel selection with quantized models on your GPU, but functionally it's supported. sometimes transcripts spell it as K V cash in logs.
[00:07:22] Sofia: any estimates on number of GPUs needed for agent assist at peak with, say, 50% cache and 180 qps?
[00:07:29] Lucas: ballpark: with a quantized 13B at ~100 tokens/request and 50% cache we approximate 9k effective tokens/sec. On A100 40GB we might get ~3-5k tokens/sec depending on kernel; so you'd need 2-3 GPUs for p95 budget. we'll size precisely after initial microbenchmarks.
[00:07:48] Aisha: we'll include several capacity options: 2 GPU (cost-optimized), 4 GPU (buffer for headroom), and dedicated pool with autoscale.
[00:07:58] [00:08:00] Speaker 3: (background noise) do we plan to instrument synthetic load to match burst patterns?
[00:08:04] Lucas: yes we will create a load harness that can replay real traces at different scale factors and also synthetic bursts. please provide a week of production traces anonymized.
[00:08:14] Daniel: can do — we'll scrub PII and share.
[00:08:18] Priya: about fallbacks — if latency spikes, can we fallback to a smaller model automatically?
[00:08:24] Lucas: yes, Redwood supports routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants by policy (latency, cost, region). we'll demo that during the POC.
[00:08:33] Sofia: how do we measure quality regressions automatically? we have a set of regression prompts.
[00:08:39] Aisha: Redwood Optimize can tie regression alerts to prompt sets/evals. we'll run baseline evals and compare each model run, surface deltas.
[00:08:47] [00:09:00] Speaker 1: (softly) what about network egress for hosted?
[00:09:03] Aisha: we'd avoid hosted for regulated data; hosted option would redacted data or use dedicated private tenancy, but it seems you want on-prem.
[00:09:12] Lucas: next, can you share current latency and error rates for your existing microservice to baseline improvement?
[00:09:18] Sofia: currently p95 ~ 700ms for our rule-based retrieval + external lookups. error/fallback around 5%. target is to reduce latency and false positives.
[00:09:28] Lucas: Good baseline. For the POC we'll instrument both token-level metrics and end-to-end.
[00:09:34] Priya: For acceptance at the end of the POC we need: 1) p95 < 350ms for 2-week steady run at simulated peak, 2) quality metrics above thresholds, 3) documented runbook and cost estimate.
[00:09:46] Aisha: We'll write those into the SOW.
[00:09:50] [00:10:00] Lucas: On the benchmark plan we'll need: sample prompts, production traces, hardware access for on-prem run (ssh/jumphost or we can run with your ops), and a test account with RBAC.
[00:10:12] Daniel: we can provide a jumpbox and temporary service account. ops will coordinate.
[00:10:18] Sofia: any privacy concerns with the evaluation data?
[00:10:22] Aisha: we'll sign an NDA if needed; for the POC you can also provide synthetic or redacted traces. plus we support customer-managed KMS.
[00:10:31] [00:10:45] Speaker 2: do you have examples of similar bank POCs?
[00:10:49] Aisha: yes – we ran a similar POC with Luminex a year ago, we can share an anonymized benchmark sheet and architecture notes.
[00:10:56] Sofia: timeline recap?
[00:10:59] Aisha: Week 1: SOW signed, infra access + traces delivered; Week 2: run microbenchmarks and model tuning; Week 3: stability runs and quality evals; Week 4: run decision review and handoff docs.
[00:11:12] Daniel: sounds good, we aim to have infra ready by 2027-01-22.
[00:11:16] Lucas: For the measurement matrix we'll capture: qps, concurrent in-flight requests, tokens per second, model latency (per-token and end-to-end), p50/p95/p99, cache hit rate, GPU utilization, and cost per 1000 tokens.
[00:11:33] Priya: can we get a simple initial estimate today? like cost buckets?
[00:11:37] Aisha: rough back-of-envelope: hosted with a managed 13B quantized option might be ~ $X per million tokens (we won't give exact in call), on-prem CAPEX depends on GPUs; we'll send detailed pricing in SOW.
[00:11:50] [00:12:05] Lucas: any regulatory red flags we should know now? data residency, retention windows, special audit needs?
[00:12:10] Sofia: retention max 90 days for logs, some conversations flagged for 7 years (audit). we need to ensure logs can be exported to archival systems and be queryable.
[00:12:20] Aisha: we can export logs to S3-compatible storage, and support configurable retention.
[00:12:25] [00:12:35] Speaker 1: (typing) ok.
[00:12:40] Lucas: I'll outline the benchmark harness and share the initial config (models, batch sizes, concurrency curves). We'll also include cache TTL experiments.
[00:12:49] Priya: Great. Are there any red flags on our side?
[00:12:52] Daniel: only timing and hardware provisioning — we want to keep the POC cost predictable.
[00:12:57] Aisha: we'll include fixed-scope options and an optional scale test add-on.
[00:13:02] [00:13:10] Sofia: One more question — can Redwood handle function/tool calling and structured output? we need structured JSON responses for downstream systems.
[00:13:17] Lucas: yes, Redwood's API supports structured outputs and tool-calling patterns, and we can validate schema during evaluation. sometimes the transcript auto-tags function call as "tool-calling" in notes.
[00:13:28] Aisha: Ok, recap of next steps: 1) Aisha send SOW + pricing + security packet; 2) Lucas send benchmark spreadsheet + harness and sample config; 3) Montara to send anonymized traces + grant jumpbox access; 4) schedule on-prem benchmark for week of 2027-01-25.
[00:13:47] Priya: confirm — we want to kick off as soon as SOW signed.
[00:13:51] Aisha: yep.
[00:13:55] Lucas: we'll try to run a small quick sanity benchmark earlier if infra is available.
[00:13:59] [00:14:10] Speaker 2: (laugh) thanks all.
